note: Hand-curated index of the pymaxim lab notebook (docs/experiments/). Status uses the verdict vocabulary of the notebook's 2026-09-13 status audit; the linked record wins if the two ever disagree.

lines.title: Survival and learned fear
lines.intro: Learning from the world's own pain rather than a teacher's credit: a drowning fear learned in Minecraft, shared between agents, carried to a second pool, and priced in a survival benchmark.

lines.title: Sharing a learned want (the Oasis)
lines.intro: Whether one agent's taught want can be exported as a signed bundle and change an independent agent's first choice — and what pooling many learners costs.

lines.title: Orienting on the Reachy Mini
lines.intro: Substrate-primary learning on a physical robot: turn toward a sound, by how much, with which joint — and whether a want taught in simulation reads out on the hardware.

lines.title: The Cradle: caregiver-taught learning
lines.intro: Developmental simulations with no LLM in the action path: an infant learns to orient because a mother's feeding relieves its hunger.

lines.title: LLM prior vs. carried substrate
lines.intro: Whether carried experience can beat a language model's prior. With the LLM choosing actions, the prior won; with the LLM removed from selection, the substrate learned a narrow preference.

lines.title: The Roy harness and EC drift
lines.intro: The three-arm method for telling substrate transfer apart from LLM role-play, and the run of mostly-null iterations that traced the gap to encoder and EC drift.

lines.title: Cross-session recall
lines.intro: The headline claim at its base: memory persists across sessions and can shift behavior. The 1.0 graduation gate came back partial.

lines.title: Mechanism and integration checks
lines.intro: Early sweeps and proofs of concept: the substrate mechanisms (P0–P8) validated one at a time, and the SEM, imagination, deliberation and embodiment pipelines wired end to end.

lines.title: Grounded language: entry audits
lines.intro: Measurements with no pass/fail gate that decide whether a grounded-language line has any data to stand on. Nothing here is a result.

experiments.title: Cross-context readout: does the nursery-taught want survive on the robot?
experiments.summary: A want taught in simulation read out on the physical robot: taught 1.00 vs satiated 0.00 and no-feed 0.50 (53b, R1 replication). Exp 53's larger step overshot — APPARATUS. n = 3/arm.
experiments.finding: 53b EARNED (delta 0.30 rad): the Exp 52 Phase B infants' persisted NAc+EC, loaded unchanged onto the physical Reachy Mini with nothing crediting on the robot, read out as taught 1.00/1.00/1.00 delivered directedness (36/36 toward, chosen direction 36/36), satiated 0.00 (no action 36/36), no_feed 0.50 (turn_right 54/54, zero learned bias). Gate I 3/3, 120/120 live percepts pattern-complete across both runs. Exp 53 (delta 0.55 rad) recorded the pre-registered APPARATUS verdict: direction 36/36 but delivered 0.75 per seed, every miss the -0.2 target (overshoot) — the finding that motivated 53b's one declared change. Readout, not learning; one session, one room, n = 3 seeds/arm, fixed step, front hemisphere; the exploratory +0.2 placement turns the wrong way 18/18 (predicted pre-data: the three-bin representation's centre bin, -0.4..+0.3, carries turn_left); nothing about magnitude or loudness. Re-validated on the robot 2026-09-02 post-D53 with the original agent files SHA-verified unchanged: reproduced exactly (taught 1.00 / satiated 0.00 / no_feed 0.50, Gate I PASS, +0.2 wrong-way 9/9, -0.6 toward 9/9). Caveat that travels with it: 85 actuator-degradation warnings across 180 trials, all roll/pitch and never yaw, the axis azimuth readout rides on - a PASS on a platform that was warning; roll/pitch recalibration owed before the next hardware block.

experiments.title: Nurture: caregiver-taught orienting through hunger relief
experiments.summary: An infant learns to orient only when feeding relieves hunger: taught 0.878 vs satiated 0.441 and no-feed 0.413 (12 seeds/arm), reproduced on re-run. Supersedes Exp 48.
experiments.finding: COMPLETE, EARNED — PASS on both pre-registered phases. Phase A (scripted, 8 seeds x 600 ticks): taught 0.892 vs satiated / yoked / no_feed 0.496 — a feed without need had zero effect. Phase B (embodied cradle_mother, apparatus v3 with shuffled stimulus order, 12 seeds/arm): taught late 0.878 vs satiated 0.441 (fed 35% of turns, credited 0%) vs no_feed 0.413 — LEARNED, MOTHER-TAUGHT and HUNGER-NECESSARY pass under gate v3 with the L2 apparatus check clean. Supersedes Exp 48. One session, n = 12/arm; sign-only relief credit discriminates nonzero-from-zero relief, not hungry-vs-sated. Re-validated 2026-09-02 post-D53: Phase B re-run whole under the same frozen gate reproduced GRADUATE (taught 0.837 / satiated 0.413 / no_feed 0.413, deltas inside the per-seed SD). One sentence of the original is retracted: per-seed values are not reproducible run-to-run (4 of 36 cells identical; per-seed r = +0.66 / +0.29 / -0.24), so the 'one weak seed' explanation is withdrawn; arm means replicate, per-seed narratives do not.

experiments.title: H2 loudness bench: is sound level readable on the live rig?
experiments.summary: Sound level is one daemon read away on the live Reachy Mini. A bench note, not a result; loudness salience was deferred and hasn't shipped.
experiments.finding: Bench note, not a behavioral result: one 75 s trace on the live Reachy Mini shows the XVF3800's pre-AGC speech energy and the AGC gain readback are both served by the daemon's existing REST parameter endpoint, so a level is one read away. Loudness / onset salience is NOT part of 1.1; the design was deferred and neither 1.1.1 nor 1.1.2 shipped it.

experiments.title: Re-adaptation after plant change (savings + learned non-use)
experiments.summary: Designed, not run: does an orient policy trained on the old robot show savings on replaced hardware? Waits on the healthy-hardware baseline.
experiments.finding: Pre-registered, no results yet: asks whether an orient policy trained on the pre-repair robot shows motor-adaptation-style savings on replaced hardware. Runs strictly after the healthy-hardware H1 baseline, whose measured constants filled the single permitted amendment slot.

experiments.title: Two-joint centering: does the runtime use body turns appropriately?
experiments.summary: Head-only agents cannot center sounds past the neck limit (0/10); body-turning agents can. The LLM crosses the front/back fold; the substrate is ~20× faster where its policy applies.
experiments.finding: COMPLETE, all three hypotheses met: a head-only agent cannot center sounds past the neck limit (0/10) while motor-bound agents can, the LLM chose a direction-correct first body turn in 10/10 trials, and measured relief credit matched true direction-progress on both arms (1.00 LLM, 0.969 substrate). The front/back fold splits the two intelligences — the LLM crosses it, the substrate is ~20x faster where its policy applies.

experiments.title: Cradle-mother seam
experiments.summary: Superseded by Exp 52. The mother effect re-earned on a corrected apparatus, but the learning gate failed; its earlier headline numbers are retired.
experiments.finding: Superseded by Exp 52 (2026-08-25). Re-baselined onto a corrected apparatus: the mother effect re-earned, but LEARNED-v2 failed and the sweep pointed to credit-tipped phase locking, not graded orienting. Its earlier headline numbers are retired. Kept as the apparatus case study; its PARTIAL stands for the constant-credit apparatus.

experiments.title: Substrate counterfactual: pilot shakedown
experiments.summary: Pilot, one seed per arm — not a result. Found a name-mismatched control and non-independent axes, so the Exp 44 confirmatory campaign is not frozen.
experiments.finding: PILOT, explicitly not a result — one seed per arm. The shakedown found the transplant control is name-mismatched and that the two reported axes encode the same entity/affordance pair rather than independent effects, so the Exp 44 confirmatory campaign is not frozen. S4 non-stationarity measurement (2026-08-24, descriptive, one seed per arm): the treatment is not stationary within a run — in every arm the non-target tools' reward bands fall from strongly to mildly rewarding by the second half while the target holds — and the free determinism probe found 0 flips on 11 identical-prompt pairs.

experiments.title: Substrate-primary preference: re-validation after the drive-pain fold
experiments.summary: Exp 42 holds after the drive-pain refactor: 40 sub-sims, none failed. The metric is saturated, so a re-run shows "not broken", not "not degraded".
experiments.finding: The Exp 42 graduation holds after the channel-split drive-pain fold: 40 sub-sims, 0 failed, discrimination reproduced identically. Caveat carried forward — the preference metric is saturated (SD 0.000), so a green re-run means 'not broken' and cannot detect a moderate regression.

experiments.title: Does a learned substrate steer the LLM? (trajectory-matched counterfactual)
experiments.summary: Exploratory: a counterbalanced positive at modest N, not a result. The 44b pilot then found flaws in the control, so the confirmatory run is not frozen.
experiments.finding: EXPLORATORY, not a graduated result. Arm A and the counterbalance completed, but modest N and residual-color caveats stand, and the 44b pilot later found a name-mismatched transplant control and non-independent axes. Read alongside 44b; the confirmatory campaign is not frozen.

experiments.title: Orient magnitude S4: population-vector readout
experiments.summary: A population-vector readout resolved the magnitude ceiling 45d found, on the live robot with no LLM. One seed; multi-seed replication outstanding.
experiments.finding: COMPLETE on live Reachy Mini with no LLM in the action path: a population-vector readout resolves the single-far-bin cell-starvation ceiling that 45d characterized. The fix is readout-independent — it bootstraps exploration into the starved cell, after which plain argmax reads the correct magnitude. n=1 (seed 3); multi-seed replication outstanding.

experiments.title: Orient magnitude: replication + cross-session transfer
experiments.finding: On live Reachy Mini, the substrate-primary magnitude policy replicates at 0.75-1.00 (mode 0.75) across seeds and transfers to a fresh hardware session without degradation.

experiments.title: Habituation: a novel sound in a wall of noise
experiments.summary: A habituating agent picks out a novel sound among 40 background noises; non-habituating controls sit at chance. Scripted and deterministic.
experiments.finding: A habituating agent reliably detects a novel sound amid 40 competing background noises while non-habituating controls perform at chance, showing familiarity-based noise suppression is essential for salience detection.

experiments.title: Operant orient: a mother teaches, a creche pools
experiments.summary: Scripted: a hungry infant with no orient drive learns to turn toward sound from a feeding mother, and twelve infants pool their policies into one.
experiments.finding: A hungry infant with no intrinsic orienting drive learns to turn toward sound purely through operant conditioning by a feeding mother, and twelve sample-limited infants federate their policies into one full-experience policy.

experiments.title: Orient magnitude: derived bin boundary
experiments.finding: The 45b ceiling was representational, not motivational: a derived bin boundary that fixed the state representation took magnitude from 0.75 to 1.00.

experiments.title: Orient magnitude: how far, not just which way
experiments.summary: On the robot, the substrate learned to size turns to target distance without overshooting — magnitude score 0.75 from relief credit alone, no LLM.
experiments.finding: The substrate learned to size rotation actions to target distance and not to overshoot, hitting the pre-registered magnitude score of 0.75 from relief-based credit alone with no LLM, effort cost, or new mechanism.

experiments.title: Substrate-native orienting, live on hardware
experiments.summary: On the physical robot, no LLM choosing actions: learned to orient in ~10 trials and kept it across sessions. The merge arm was later downgraded (a vacuous guard, D62).
experiments.finding: All three pre-registered arms passed: the substrate learned a real-hardware closed-loop orientation policy from zero in ~10 trials, persisted it across sessions, and merged learners; a head-frame bug affected magnitude estimates but not directional learning.

experiments.title: Operant gaze + substrate generalization
experiments.summary: Simulation feasibility study: on unseen individuals a lookup table hits chance while the EC substrate transfers at 0.938. No production behavior claim.
experiments.finding: Sim feasibility study for Maxim's first job: a dict lookup hits chance (-0.005) on unseen individuals while the EntorhinalCortex substrate reaches 0.938 transfer accuracy, so the substrate's decisive advantage is visual-category generalization to novel instances.

experiments.title: Substrate-primary exploration: override its own prior?
experiments.finding: VOID. The mechanism operated, but the experiment could not isolate exploration and the primary metric floored, so no claim is drawn from it. Exp 42 asked the question in a form that could be answered.

experiments.title: Counter-prior in the Goldilocks zone (Qwen-32B)
experiments.summary: Null. On the one model where a substrate effect had shown, a wrong prior still won: burned agents warmed at the deceptive hearth as readily as fresh ones.
experiments.finding: Even in the one model where substrate effects were previously detected, the agent carrying cross-session burn memory warmed at the hearth as readily as a fresh agent, showing prior-dominance holds and substrate effects depend on task-prior alignment rather than model scale.

experiments.title: Cross-model results
experiments.summary: Partial. Four open-model runs complete; the cloud arm was deferred. Substrate visibility depends on prior headroom; R1-Distill gave the first clean Wire-A ablation.
experiments.finding: PARTIAL (pymaxim audit 2026-09-13): four open-source-model fires complete; the cloud-model arm was deferred and is not a result. Substrate visibility is Goldilocks-dependent; the R1 variant produced the first clean Wire-A attribution.

experiments.title: Counter-prior substrate
experiments.summary: Null. Across four frontier models, agents carrying pain from a deceptive hearth kept the wrong fire→warm prior. Carried state did not override it.
experiments.finding: Across four frontier models, agents carrying cross-session pain from a deceptive hearth kept the wrong fire->warm prior and continued engaging the harmful entity, showing substrate state transfer does not override deeply embedded LLM priors.

experiments.title: Cross-session graduation (1.0 gate)
experiments.summary: Partial. A cross-session behavioral shift appears at ≥32B, but the isolation arm failed wherever the primary passed, and the magnitudes did not reproduce later (L8).
experiments.finding: PARTIAL, an investigation gate: the cross-session behavioral delta appears at >=32B scale but the Arm C isolation test failed on every model where the primary metric passed, so independence from the LLM prior is not established. Limit L8 (2026-08-22): the identical commit on the identical seeds does not reproduce its own June result (0.42 then, 0.71 now) — the recorded magnitudes are readings taken at one time, not constants.

experiments.title: Roy-5b confound isolation
experiments.summary: The EC drift fix (threshold 0.40 → 0.44), not the naming-event scaffold, closed Roy-5b's recognition gap. Whether that changes behavior was left open. Supersedes Roy-5b.
experiments.finding: Branch A decisive: the EC drift fix (threshold 0.40 → 0.44) is the dominant cause of Roy-5b's gap closure on the recognition metric (EC node overlap); the naming-event scaffold contributes zero. Whether it changes behavior was left open — Exp 27 found the drift fix did not change Roy-2c's behavior. Supersedes Roy-5b's reading.

experiments.title: Roy-5b
experiments.summary: Superseded by Exp 36. A conditional pass at the time — pre-registered row 1 passed, with the EC-drift confound unresolved; Exp 36 showed the scaffold wasn't the cause.
experiments.finding: Superseded by Roy-5b confound isolation (Exp 36). At the time: a conditional pass — the literal pre-registered row 1 passed, but on a (drive, drive) intra-modal edge with the EC-drift confound unresolved. Exp 36 then showed the EC drift fix, not the naming-event scaffold, closed the gap. The conditional pass stands as recorded; it is not evidence for the scaffold.

experiments.title: Roy-1a
experiments.summary: Null. Priming wrote substrate state that carried forward, but the LLM-primary proposer never used it — a structural signal, not a behavioral one.
experiments.finding: NULL (pymaxim audit 2026-09-13). experiments.title: Substrate-primary preference
experiments.summary: With no LLM choosing actions, the substrate learned from pain to prefer the safe warmth source (0.98, 10 seeds/arm) and tracked a swap. Narrow, near-deterministic.
experiments.finding: GRADUATE, and the strongest substrate-primary result in the set: with no LLM in the action path, the substrate learns from embodied pain to prefer the safe warmth source (0.984 / 0.975 across 10 seeds per arm) and tracks the contingency when the counterbalance swaps which source is safe. The gating-OFF ablation graduated identically, which attributes the effect to per-source credit assignment rather than the drive-gating heuristic. Scope: mechanism-level, near-deterministic.

experiments.title: Four-arm sharing benchmark: a taught want transfers between independent agents
experiments.summary: One agent's taught want, shared as a signed bundle, changed an independent agent's first choice: 0.80 vs a 0.00 floor, n = 50/arm. Transfer, not generalization.
experiments.finding: EARNED — the 1.2 "Oasis" headline. Agent A's teacher-taught, world-keyed operant bias, exported as a signed bundle and ingested into an independent agent B (different agent_id, separately built EC + SensorEncoder, disjoint cluster ids), changes B's FIRST-contact choice. Live Paper 1.16.5 Minecraft world (not the mock), n = 50 receivers/arm, substrate-primary. Taught raw 0.84 [0.71, 0.92] and 0.80 bias-decisive vs isolated floor 0.22 raw / 0.00 decisive; satiated (zero-credit donor) 0.12 and dangling-half falsifier 0.12, both at floor. All four gates PASS: TRANSFERRED 0.80 >= 0.70, ABOVE-FLOOR 0.62 >= 0.20, WANT-NOT-FILE 0.72 >= 0.20, BOTH-HALVES -0.10 < 0.10, plus the anti-vacuity kit. 40 of 50 taught first contacts decided by the situation-keyed learned-bias channel. Scope: one campaign, one world layout, teacher-taught wants — not scaling (Exp 57), not hardware, not aversion, not cross-layout (R1). Re-baselined 2026-09-19 on Paper 1.20.4 (RB-1): PASS, every rate identical to the 1.16.5 campaign — a same-seed reproduction on the new platform, not an independent replication; one duplicated row from an operator restart is disclosed in the file and moves no gate.

experiments.title: Dose-response ladder: pooling scales per-agent learning, at a total-experience cost
experiments.summary: Partial by design. Pooling cut per-agent trials to criterion (21 → 10.5, p ≈ 1e-4), but the pool spent more total experience than one agent given it all.
experiments.finding: PARTIAL by pre-registration — the 1.2 scaling claim, run as its may-fail second claim; both halves are load-bearing. MONOTONICITY (primary) PASS in its robust form: per-agent trials-to-criterion fall 21 / 21 / 15.5 / 10.5 across N = 1/2/4/8 (Jonckheere-Terpstra permutation p ~ 1e-4, surviving the drop-censored-rungs guard), driven by endpoint coverage widening 0.25 -> 0.50 -> 0.75 -> 0.75 — a lone agent never reaches the 3-of-4 criterion in 20 trials, an agent in a creche of 8 reaches it in ~10.5 of its own. NOT-JUST-MORE-DATA FAIL: N x tau = 42 / 62 / 84 vs a matched single agent's 41 / 46 / 43, so the pool spends MORE total experience than one agent given all of it — convex-combination merge overhead, named as the 1.3 audit target. Collective learning is a per-participant win, not a total-sample free lunch. Live Minecraft, 4 rungs x 3 conditions x 20 cohorts (9,200 rows), substrate-primary. Not a scaling law; the failing gate is the strict serial sample-cost comparison, not wall-clock.

experiments.title: Cross-layout generalization: a structural null (representation vs cache)
experiments.summary: Null. The shared want is an exact-key cache: a genuinely different layout misses it. Transfer is shown; generalization is not.
experiments.finding: CACHE-CONFIRMED (structural null). Asks whether Exp 56's shared want carries a generalizable representation or a cached association: does a want taught at one world layout fire at a layout the receiver never trained on? It does not — the shared want is an exact-key cluster cache with no cross-layout generalization channel, knowable from the substrate mechanism without a live campaign. Bounds the 1.2 headline: transfer is demonstrated, generalization is not. A 1.3 readout design target, not a defect; a null shipped as a null.

experiments.title: Premise check: do the world-owned drives move behaviour? (a null)
experiments.summary: Null. The game's drives don't move behavior toward eating or healing; the survival loop has three breaks, which became the 1.3 build list.
experiments.finding: PREMISE-NULL. The minecraft_player world-owned drives (health homeostatic, food entropic, both drift_rate 0.0 — the game drains them, not the model) do not measurably move behaviour toward the corrective affordances, and the survival loop has three specific breaks. Per the rung's own pre-registered stop rule the dependent survival rungs R3/R4 do not run in 1.2; the three breaks become the 1.3 build list rather than a benchmark back-fitted onto a premise that does not hold. A null shipped as a null.

experiments.title: Drowning avoidance: learned, anticipatory fear from the game's own pain
experiments.summary: An agent held underwater until it hurt learned to leave the water before the pain: 1.0 vs 0.0 for its yoked twin without the fear wire (5 seeds/arm, p = 1/252).
experiments.finding: EARNED — the Wire-4 situation-fear mechanism's behavioural graduation, and the first Maxim result whose learning signal is the WORLD's rather than a teacher's. An agent held underwater until air-hunger pain, then rescued, books a fear keyed to the underwater situation and on later submersions leaves the water BEFORE the pain would fire; its yoked twin with the same pain exposure but the fear subscriber detached never does. Live Paper 1.20.4 water classroom, substrate-primary (no LLM in the action path), 5 seeds/arm, 6 pain-free placements per probe. All five frozen gates PASS: FEAR post P(surface) median 1.0 (from 0.0 pre, every seed) vs ABLATED 0.0 (zero executor calls in 30/30), exact permutation p = 1/252 (the floor for 5 v 5), specificity water fear -1.0 vs shore 0.0 on every seed. Latency to air median 1.72 s, inside the 4.34 s US-free window. Caveat recorded: after a seed's first escape the action also carries a positive causal link, so the fear-only read is the FIRST post placement per seed (5/5 surfaced, 2.9-3.3 s). Planned as 'dark = danger' and BLOCKED at the instrument (Exp 58) — the cue was swapped to water, which separates.

experiments.title: Shared survival fear: a learned fear transfers between independent agents
experiments.summary: A learned drowning fear, shared as a bundle, sent receivers out of the water on first contact: 12/12 vs 0/24 isolated (p = 8e-10). One donor, one campaign.
experiments.finding: EARNED — the 1.3 "Oasis-2" headline. A donor learns the drowning fear the hard way, exports its substrate through the shipped signed-bundle path, and a fresh receiver ingests it (discounted x0.75 at the ingest bound — vicarious fear is real and weaker than direct), reboots, and leaves the water on its FIRST loop-live submersion having never felt the pain. One campaign at one code hash, 121 rows, zero refusals: 12/12 transferred receivers vs 0/24 isolated, 0/12 cluster-not-fear (the ablated donor's cluster and percept valence shipped, the fear did not) and 0/24 dangling (fear dropped at ingest for want of its world node); Fisher one-sided p = 8.0e-10; all six frozen gates PASS. The loop-OFF representation gate read the discounted fear (-0.75) exactly on every receiver before any loop ran. NOT earned: extinction, scaling past one donor, a received fear's reach to another pool (Exp 62 tested only the agent's own fear), hive-side promotion.

experiments.title: Survival benchmark: what a carried drive buys at the lethal moment
experiments.summary: A benchmark, nothing graduated. A carried fear cut median time to air from 28 s to ~3 s. Everyone survived — the fear buys cost, not life.
experiments.finding: An INSTRUMENT and a frozen baseline — nothing graduated. Five arms x 12 fresh agents, one unrescued submersion each on a depth-calibrated frozen gauntlet. Median time to air: A innate reflex only 28.0 s, B learns the fear in situ 8.6 s, C carries a self-learned fear 3.2 s, D carries a RECEIVED fear (the Exp 61 receiver) 3.1 s, E same pain exposure as C with the fear subscriber detached 28.1 s. Every agent in every arm survived — with regeneration on, survival is a declared CEILING and separates nothing. What the drive buys is the cost it removes: ~25 s of latency, ~11 hp and ~22 s of oxygen pain — NOT life. E == A (exposure without the subscriber buys nothing); D == C (the discounted vicarious fear escapes like the self-learned one, p 0.84). Reported with its instrument trouble in the open: the frozen report read INCOMPLETE on two rules that were facts about the instrument (a code-hash rule no bench could satisfy; a tick-period band that measured phase rather than cadence on few-second events); both amended post-data, instrument-only, two-lens reviewed, and published BESIDE the frozen report. The frozen band had refused the carried-fear arm's fastest rows, so restoring them moved that median 0.10 s in the claim's direction — the amendment rests on the instrument argument, not the rows' outcomes.

experiments.title: Cross-pool readout: a learned fear carries to a second pool on the shipped body
experiments.summary: Rung A: a fear learned in one pool carried to a second pool, 12/12 (lower bound 0.758) vs ablated 0/3. Invariance to place, not to a changed situation.
experiments.finding: Rung A EARNED, the day after 1.3.0 shipped, on the shipped minecraft_player body with no mechanism change, no new sensor and no ingest. An agent that learned the drowning fear in pool 1 left the water on its first live submersion in pool 2 (different altitude and spawn distance): cross-pool 12/12 (Wilson lower bound 0.758 — the interval is the number, not 100%), same-pool 12/12, fear-ablated 0/3 with zero executor calls; five frozen gates PASS; Fisher one-sided cross v ablated p = 0.0022. The ablated agents resolve to the SAME node with fear 0, so the contrast is the fear alone. NOT a general generalization result: one discriminating world sensor (is_in_water, binary), a two-point situation space; what carried is invariance to place, not to a changed situation. The context wall stands and was measured: a lit pond reads 0.588 against the 0.85 threshold. The 0.799 'night pool' reading was corrected 2026-09-25 to the time_of_day wrap (#899): midnight reads 0.903, and the fear misses only in roughly the last 5% of each in-game day. Bounded to the sealed-shell, frozen-day pool class. The agent's OWN fear — a received fear's reach to another pool is untested. Rung B is designed, not built.

experiments.title: Nurture on the robot's own body
experiments.summary: Phase A only: the Exp 52 nursery on the robot's own body earned (taught 0.858 vs 0.472 satiated). The hardware readout phases haven't run.
experiments.finding: Phase A EARNED; Phases B (readout on the physical Reachy) and C (the user path) have not run. The Exp 52 nursery re-run on the robot's own body and action keys: taught late 0.858 vs satiated 0.472 and no_feed 0.514 — mother-taught +0.34, hunger-necessary +0.39, all pre-registered gates, 12 seeds/arm. Magnitude NOT resolved: the taught agents prefer the normal step in every bin. The prerequisite for sharing a taught want on hardware.

experiments.title: Survival wants: learned dark-fear (blocked at the instrument)
experiments.summary: Null with cause: danger and safety never formed distinct world clusters, so the fear had nothing to key on. The fear's read path was never shown live. Exp 60 re-ran it on water.
experiments.finding: NULL-WITH-CAUSE (instrument-blocked). The fear's write side worked live — pain wrote a fear onto the world cluster — but the danger and safe situations never formed distinct world clusters under light, depth, or depth plus a hostile mob, so the fear had nothing to key on. The loop-executed read was never shown live on this line (correction 2026-09-16: the staircase flee was a preflight actuation check, not the agent loop). No behavioural claim. Exp 60 re-ran the question on a cue that does separate: water.

experiments.title: Learned-bias pre-registration (v1): does relief teach eating when hungry?
experiments.summary: Superseded without data: the design was caught confounded pre-data, and the question was resolved offline.
experiments.finding: Superseded without data (pymaxim audit 2026-09-13). The raw-flip design was caught confounded pre-data and replaced by v2; the question was then resolved offline — the cluster credit is a behavioural messenger, not a cause.

experiments.title: Learned-bias v2: does drive-relief credit make eating state-contingent?
experiments.finding: Superseded at the design-review gate; no harness was built and no data taken. Its reasoning is kept in the design review.

experiments.title: Paired-data audit: is there sensor-and-text data to learn language from?
experiments.summary: No gate. One committed trace pairs sensors with text, and it has 11 word types — too thin for grounded language. The data source was redesigned.
experiments.finding: A measurement with no pass/fail gate. Of 187 committed data files, one pairs world snapshots with text; that trace has 3 text templates, 11 word types and 3 world clusters — too thin for the grounded-language line. The owner chose to redesign the data source.

experiments.title: Paired-data re-audit: the redesigned source
experiments.finding: Same script on a redesigned, operator-staged trace: 4 templates, 19 word types, 12 world clusters. Recorded as a post-null change of source, not a pass; no gate applied.
